conviction_note: The fundamental read leans slightly negative. Q4 adjusted EBITDA has to step up from $35.0M to the guide-implied $43-47M while energy storage is guided to stay delayed, US casketed deaths fell in the same quarter and copper set records. The new CEO's first FY27 guide is set against a street that appears to expect about +55% EPS growth. The other side is a crowded short (16% of shares out, 10 days to cover), a stock 4% above its 52-week low that fell 14% on the last print, a dividend raise declared the day before the release, and chairman buying. So p_up sits only a little under 50 (46) and abs_move is 7, well above the 2.28 median, because a first guide under a new CEO plus a strategic-review update is a guidance-scale event, as in Aug 2026 (-14.3%) and Feb 2025 (-9.9%). The findings sum to -0.5 and the scaled number to -0.56; the two agree.

It will be the first guide from a CEO who started 2026-08-31, after two FY26 cuts. Energy storage delays were guided to last through FY26 with improvement 'anticipated in 2027', and casketed-death and input-cost headwinds continue (SCI, copper). That leans toward a guide at or below a street that looks like it expects a large FY27 recovery.

findings.finding: Matthews will likely give its first FY27 outlook with this release, from a CEO who joined from Lincoln Electric on 2026-08-31. The street appears to carry FY27 EPS of about $0.79: a forward P/E of 24.39 at $19.19 implies it, against FY26 consensus of $0.51, so roughly +55%. The company cut FY26 twice, guides energy storage delays through FY26 with improvement only 'anticipated in 2027', and still faces casketed-death and input-cost headwinds. A first-time CEO setting a conservative base below that street number is the more likely direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance resets drove the two largest reactions in the baseline: -14.32% on 2026-08-07 (FY26 EBITDA cut from at least $180M to $158-162M) and -9.91% on 2025-02-07. The Nov 2025 print that set the FY26 guide moved -1.48% / -0.57%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stale targets ($31.33 mean) and a forward P/E of 24 on FY27 numbers show the street has not rebased FY27 to the new CEO's view. If it had, FY27 EPS would sit near FY26 and the forward P/E would read above 30. Against that, the 16% short interest says part of the buy side is already positioned for another reset.
findings.independence: The headwinds come from the company's own Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000063296/000006329626000074/ex991_3q2026earningspr.htm) and SCI's Q3 volumes (separate finding). The FY27 street number is inferred from a single aggregator's forward P/E, so the size is capped small.

findings.finding: Q4 arithmetic from the company's own numbers: the FY26 guide of $158-162M less 9M adjusted EBITDA of $114.955M requires $43.0-47.0M in Q4, against $35.0M in Q3 and $44.7M in Q2. A segment build gives about $44M: Memorialization about $44.5M (Q3 $42.2M plus the Q3-to-Q4 seasonal step of +$2.3M seen in FY25), Propelis about $12.7M (the company's preliminary estimate of the 40% share, booked one quarter in arrears), corporate about -$11.5M, and Industrial Technologies at about -$2M. That needs IT to improve from -$5.4M while energy storage is guided delayed through FY-end. The low end of the range or a small miss is the likelier outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 miss came with a guide cut and the stock fell 14.3%. Q2, where the guide was maintained, moved +0.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote the FY guide, not the implied Q4 step-up or the IT swing it needs. If this were priced, the Q4 consensus EPS of $0.28 would sit below the guide-implied level rather than on it. The finding is mostly inside what the company has guided, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same company document as the guide. The Q4 FY25 segment seasonality comes from the FY25 Q4 release (https://finviz.com/news/235477/matthews-international-reports-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-ended-september-30-2025).

findings.finding: Service Corporation International's Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep, the same months as MATW's fiscal Q4): comparable core funeral services -0.5% and atneed -1.3%, with the core cremation rate up 0.6 points to 58.2%. That implies US casketed services down roughly 2% year on year. SCI also lowered its 2026 EPS guide on 'lower funeral volumes than we originally anticipated'.
findings.link: SCI is the largest US funeral home operator and a buyer of caskets and memorials. Matthews' Memorialization segment (about 85% of Q3 sales, $208.1M of $246.0M) attributed its Q3 volume headwind to 'lower estimated U.S. casketed deaths', which SCI's casketed-service mix measures directly. The share of Matthews revenue from SCI itself was not found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Memorialization volume weakness was one of the stated causes of the Aug 2026 guide cut (-14.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer release three weeks old that no MATW preview cites. It is also a continuation of the trend Matthews already put into its August guide, which is why it is sized small. If it were unpriced news, Memorialization estimates would have moved, and no estimate revision is visible.
findings.independence: Carriage Services' Q3 (separate finding) shows the opposite at a smaller operator, so this is partly offset.

findings.finding: Carriage Services' Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep): same-store funeral contracts +2.3% after -5.8% in Q1 and -3.5% in Q2, with volumes down in July and August and up in September and October. Q4 is guided flat to +1%. Comparable cemetery preneed production fell 4.8% and interment rights sold fell 7.3%.
findings.link: Carriage is a US funeral and cemetery operator buying caskets (Matthews' casket line) and cemetery memorials (bronze and granite, Matthews' memorial line). The Matthews revenue share from Carriage was not found. Rule 5: a smaller operator than SCI.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No MATW reaction tied to a Carriage print was found. Carriage itself fell 21.6% on this release.
findings.why_not_priced: It cuts both ways. The September-October funeral rebound is a mild support for Matthews' FY27 casket commentary, and the cemetery preneed slump is a headwind for memorials. Net zero, filed for the judges.
findings.independence: SCI shows flat-to-down volumes for the same months (finding above). Different operator, different document.

findings.finding: COMEX copper set successive records during Matthews' fiscal Q4: a prior high on Aug 12, $6.727/lb on Aug 27, and about $6.80/lb on Sep 8, still near $6.70 on Sep 25. Bronze memorials are mostly copper, and Matthews already cited 'input costs escalating beyond inflationary price increases' when it cut the guide on Aug 6.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Input-cost pressure was one of the stated causes of the Aug 2026 cut (-14.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: Copper was already near records when the guide was set, so the further rise after Aug 6 was only a few percent. Matthews' hedging and pricing pass-through are unknown, so this is a proxy and sized small.
findings.independence: The EW preview (2026-11-11) cites copper at $4.50-6.60/lb and steel up 21% as cost pressure. Different source, same macro series.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-01 (8-K filed 09-04) Matthews signed a Ninth Amendment to its credit agreement. It sets a covenant relief period to 2027-12-31 with maximum leverage of 5.25x for the quarters through Jun 2027, stepping down to 4.75x and then 4.50x. It excludes the Propelis 40% stake from the leverage ratio, cuts the revolver from $700M to $650M and removes the $350M foreign borrowing facility. What the money buys: covenant headroom, not a ramp. Net debt was $529.7M at Q3 against an ex-Propelis EBITDA run rate of roughly $115-120M, so about 4.5x against a 2.5x target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior financing-led print reaction found. The stock drifted from about $22 to $20 in the week after the 8-K (chairman purchase prices of $21.08 on Aug 24 and $19.99 on Sep 11).
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public, but previews quote gross debt reduction ($144M) rather than the covenant relief, which shows leverage is above where the old covenant sat. Any Q4 net debt or leverage disclosure will be read against it. The amendment also removes breach risk inside the window, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q3 release (net debt $529.7M, 9M operating cash flow -$69.5M) points the same way. Different document.

findings.finding: Mid-quarter statement, 8-K of 2026-10-01: the company restated a European engineering restructuring projected to save about $10M a year starting in fiscal 2027, confirmed the CEO change effective Aug 31, and said it 'expects to provide additional information regarding these initiatives in the coming months'. The Q3 release had said the strategic-alternatives review (J.P. Morgan advising, focused on Industrial Technologies partnerships) would run through the fourth quarter. A review update or portfolio action with this release is therefore plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 2025 warehouse-automation sale ($230M, announced with Q4 FY25) came with a -1.48% move. No clean read on portfolio actions.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews ask only about the guide and engineering orders. A concrete IT partnership or sale that delevers is not visible in a stock 4% above its low with 16% short. The sign depends on price, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: The Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000063296/000006329626000074/ex991_3q2026earningspr.htm) carries the review timing. Same company, different document.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-18, the day before the print, the board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.26 from $0.255, the 33rd consecutive increase (8-K filed 2026-11-19 at 10:01). It did so while operating under covenant relief and after 9M operating cash flow of -$69.5M. The board, with the new CEO quoted, chose not to signal cash stress going into the first FY27 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The November dividend raise is customary (Nov 2025 also raised), so the read is that a cut or freeze was not chosen.
findings.why_not_priced: It was released the morning of the print and the stock still fell 1.8% intraday to $19.19. A board that knows the Q4 numbers and the FY27 plan raising a 5.3%-yield dividend argues against a disaster reset. Because the raise is routine, it is sized small.
findings.independence: Chairman open-market purchases (separate finding) point the same way.

findings.why_not_priced: The position itself is the pricing. If the shorts had covered on a view that the reset is done, short interest would have fallen into the print, but it rose.

findings.why_not_priced: The low expectation is the price. What is not priced is the asymmetry: a release that clears a low bar has room to re-rate toward stale targets. Offset by the possibility that a new CEO resets the bar lower again (finding 1).

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The run-up is flat, and the stock sits at its lows with a crowded, growing short. The fundamental lean (Q4 step-up and FY27 reset risk) is negative, and positioning, the dividend raise and insider buying cut against it, so p_up is only 4 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short at 16% of shares out, 10 days to cover): the next-guide negative went from -2.0 to -1.2 (also rule 6, because the FY27 street bar is inferred from a single aggregator's forward P/E), the Q4 arithmetic from -1.0 to -0.7, SCI from -0.6 to -0.4 and copper from -0.4 to -0.3.
Rules 5 and 6: SCI and copper are partly inside the guide Matthews set in August (it already cited casketed deaths and input costs), which is part of why they are small.
Rule 4: the credit amendment was examined for what it buys (covenant headroom, no ramp) and kept as a small negative (-0.3).
